question: Should OpenClaw add a core child-visible pre-timeout warning/grace contract for sub-agent runs, and if so what config/tool surface and delivery semantics should native and ACP runtimes use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding this safely requires product choices about public config/API naming, defaults, per-spawn overrides, and cross-runtime lifecycle behavior that automation should not invent.

options.title: Define Core Warning Contract
options.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, and optionally a carefully named per-spawn override, with native and ACP warning delivery covered by lifecycle tests.

options.title: Keep Hard Timeout And Improve Recovery
options.body: Decline pre-timeout child warnings for now and route the user pain to post-timeout notification, durable completion delivery, and recovery issues instead.

options.title: Document Prompt-Based Checkpointing
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and document operator prompting/checkpoint guidance without adding new config or warning delivery behavior.

recommendation.title: Define Core Warning Contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, and optionally a carefully named per-spawn override, with native and ACP warning delivery covered by lifecycle tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review comments and recent sub-agent lifecycle work make this the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
